Experience in multi-INT fusion, with a SIGINT focus, and integration of national and tactical ISR sources.

Prior experience directly supporting Counterintelligence or Special Programs missions.

Develop route alignment mapping and infrastructure corridor visualization products.
Maintain geospatial records of construction progress and completed works.

Prepare graphical presentations and maps for progress meetings and client reviews.

Integrate GIS datasets with CAD and BIM environments to support project delivery.
Verify spatial accuracy of engineering and construction data.

Develop asset inventories and geospatial databases for bridge components and infrastructure systems.
Support digital handover requirements and asset management programs.
Maintain accurate records of completed infrastructure assets for future operation and maintenance.

Support digital transformation initiatives and smart infrastructure solutions.
Contribute to GIS-enabled project management and construction monitoring systems.
Assist with implementation of digital twin, BIM-GIS integration, and geospatial data visualization initiatives where applicable.

Maintain data security, version control, and document management procedures.
Participate in project audits and data reviews.

Minimum 5 years of experience on transportation, bridge, highway, or urban infrastructure projects.
Experience working within multidisciplinary engineering and construction environments.

Experience supporting client organizations, engineering consultants, or major contractors is preferred.

Excellent attention to detail and data accuracy.
Ability to transform complex geospatial information into meaningful visual outputs.

Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic project environment.

Job Description

This Opportunity

What if you could shape built and natural environments and the future of those who depend on them? At WSP, you can. WSP is currently seeking an Environmental Engineer
to join our Earth & Environment team in either Indianapolis, IN, Fort Wayne, IN, Chicago, IL, Detroit, MI, or Valparaiso, IN
. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to technically challenging site investigation and remediation projects supporting energy sector clients throughout northern Indiana.

At WSP, you'll have the opportunity to do the kind of work the world needs while collaborating with some of the brightest minds in the industry. You'll work on projects that positively impact communities and the environment while building a career as unique as you. We foster a culture that is open, curious, passionate, and adaptable, where diverse perspectives drive innovation and complex challenges inspire growth. With access to global expertise, meaningful project experiences, and opportunities for continuous development, you'll find the support and flexibility to grow your skills, expand your career, and make a lasting impact. Here, you can thrive on challenges, work alongside talented professionals, and create a future you're proud of. With us, you can

We are seeking a motivated candidate who is eager to learn and join our current multi-disciplinary team in executing technically challenging site investigation and remediation projects for our energy clients primarily in northern Indiana.

This job opening provides an opportunity to progress your career while working for an established environmental consulting firm that values employee enthusiasm, technical excellence, and professional growth. We encourage you to apply for this opportunity.

Your Impact

This position involves the implementation of project work associated with multimedia (air, water, soil, and biota) investigations and remediation. The position requires work at project sites, around construction equipment, drilling rigs, and environmental contamination. The selected candidate needs to be a self-starter, open to learning, adaptable to change, have a strong work ethic, and thrive in a dynamic environment with multiple priorities.

This position offers the opportunity to learn from and grow with an established team while addressing complex environmental challenges through the following responsibilities:

Approximately 70% field work and travel with overnight stays. Travel can include weeks at a time or a few days per week.
Perform environmental sampling (e.g., surface water, groundwater, soil, sediment, soil vapor, indoor air) and oversee subcontractors in the field (e.g., drillers).
Complete detailed field notes and other forms of documentation to accurately capture field activities and observations.
Collaborate in a team environment and communicate effectively with staff across multiple disciplines.
Communicate professionally with staff, management, clients, regulators, and on-site personnel both verbally and in writing.
Assist with project planning and coordination with laboratories, drillers, and equipment vendors.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

B.S. in Environmental Engineering or related field.
1+ years of relevant experience in environmental sampling, site investigation, or remediation.
Must be organized and detail-oriented.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Flexible to work outside normal business hours, at locations requiring overnight stays, and overtime as needed.
Ability to apply analytical and scientific thinking to define and solve problems.
Ability to work effectively in a team environment, follow detailed instructions, and learn new skills.
Ability to remain on feet for extended periods of time, either stationary or walking.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.
Must be able to pass a HAZWOPER physical and be medically able to wear a tight-fitting respirator.
Must successfully complete and pass WSP's Motor Vehicle screening.
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification required.
Experience in site investigations required.
Valid driver's license required.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience using and maintaining field equipment (e.g., groundwater pumps, field meters).
Regulatory experience in Indiana and Michigan.

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

jobs.title: Environmental Manager
jobs.description:
Work for Indiana

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About The Department Of Natural Resources (DNR)

The Indiana Department of Natural Resources protects, enhances, preserves, and wisely uses natural, cultural, and recreational resources for the benefit of Indiana's citizens through professional leadership, management, and education. The Indiana Division of Historic Preservation and Archaeology promotes the conservation of Indiana's cultural resources through public education efforts, financial incentives including several grant and tax credit programs, and the administration of state and federally mandated legislation.

Role Overview

The Historic Structures Reviewer performs regulatory reviews under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, the National Environmental Policy Act, and Sections 14, 16, and 18 of IC 14-21-1. The reviewer collaborates with government officials, staff, and the public to evaluate the effects of Federal or state actions on historic properties and seek ways to avoid, minimize and mitigate impacts to cultural resources. The Historic Structures Reviewer also participates in education and outreach to educate others about historic preservation. Applicants must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Professional Qualification Standards through a combination of education and experience in the history, architecture and/or preservation field.

Role Requirements

Bachelor or Graduate degree from an accredited university or college in historic preservation, architectural history, art history, public history, preservation law, or a closely related field.
At least two (2) years of experience in research, writing, or teaching in American architectural history or restoration architecture.
Related certifications and coursework may be considered for education or experience.
Knowledge of, and ability to apply federal and state historic preservation statutes, regulations, standards, and criteria.
Knowledge of, and ability to apply the Secretary of the Interior's "Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties" (36 C.F.R. Part 68) and applicable guidelines.
Knowledge of U.S. and Indiana history and architectural history.
Ability to interpret technical drawings, construction plans, schematics, topographic maps, and floor plans.
Ability to prepare documents for administrative and regulatory action.
Excellent research and writing skills for preparing accurate, precise, clear, and thorough reports.
Ability to respond to technical inquiries from staff, project applicants, other local state and federal agencies, consultants, and the general public
Ability to use SHAARD database of information on historical, architectural, and archaeological resources in Indiana and familiarity using GIS systems
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Be willing to travel with reasonable accommodation.

Salary

The salary for this position traditionally starts at $53,222.00 but may be commensurate with education and work experience. Use our Compensation Calculator
to view the total compensation package.

A Day In The Life

The essential functions of this role are as follows:

Serves as an environmental expert and provides guidance to regulated communities, government officials, attorneys and staff responsible for a variety of programs and program elements.
Project Management: Performs project management duties to ensure effective and timely management of program area needs, attends meetings, and responds to telephone calls, e-mails, etc., as required. Acts as a technical point-of-contact for assigned programs administering environmental programs which may include, but not limited to, environmental media sampling, data analysis, technical writing, work plan and report preparation, technical reviews, etc.
Permits: Researches state and federal guidance, laws, and regulations related to permits. Contacts applicants to request additional information to process applications, when necessary. Responds to comments from applicants, defends permit terms and conditions, and interacts with permittees to resolve permitting issues. Attends and participates in public meetings and hearings regarding permit actions throughout Indiana and/or appears in legal appeals of permit actions.
Inspection: Conducts surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, reads plans, interprets findings, and cites appropriate violations of state and federal regulations. Provides technical and regulatory guidance to the regulated community in their assigned geographic area.
Enforcement & Compliance: Uses all compliance, enforcement tools, and resources available to ensure that regulated sources return to compliance with state and federal laws, regulations, and standards in a timely manner.
Support Services: Works to support the various programs in assigned agency in multiple capacities.
Sampling: Assists with the preparation of sampling and analysis work plans. Conducts field work as necessary following agency/section Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for assigned sites.
Technical Analysis & Testing: Conducts technical analysis and/or provides technical insights to assess environmental impacts with goals to meet state and national regulations.
Outreach Coordination: Communicates effectively with responsible parties, consultants, and/or their representatives, affected stakeholders, and interested parties such as citizens, public officials, and interest groups in a courteous and professional manner regarding permits, laws, questions, and program-related inquiries.
Essential functions of this position require travel on most workdays to inspect, audit, examine, survey, or investigate clients, customers, or other regulated entities and write reports at various sites depending on business needs. Employee reports to the agency’s office for occasional meetings or events. Number and timing of work hours may vary daily or weekly to accommodate operational needs and staffing concerns at the client’s or customer’s worksite, minimize expenditures for repeated visits to complete the work, and allocate resources to complete assigned work effectively.

The job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

This position is exempt from overtime compensation for additional work hours which may be required to complete essential functions or other assigned work. Exempt employees may work more than 75 hours in a pay period without additional compensation and must report a minimum of 75 hours per pay period of work hours and/or paid leave taken to receive their base biweekly salary.

What You'll Need For Success

Individuals in this role should minimally be able to articulate or demonstrate the following:

Broad knowledge of theories, environmental protection principles and practices, specialty area, and program area.
Thorough knowledge of chemistry, biology, hydrology, mathematics, engineering, and other environmental sciences as they relate to program area.
Thorough knowledge of soil, water, air sampling, laboratory analysis and interpretation as it relates to program area.
Ability to conduct surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, read plans, interpret findings, and make recommendations.
Ability to prepare documents for administrative and regulatory action.
Excellent research and writing skills for preparing accurate, precise, clear, and thorough reports.
Ability to effectively interact and orally communicate with parties with diverse levels of environmental expertise particularly for purposes of meetings, hearings, and negotiating critically sensitive issues.
Ability to interpret and apply legal terminology and practices, and the ability to apply these in a variety of conditions and situations.

A degree is not required. However, at least five (5) years of environmental or environmental public health experience applying the outlined knowledge, skills, and abilities in a similar role may be considered.

Individuals should have the ability to perform essential functions with or without reasonable accommodation.

Supervisory Responsibilities/Direct Reports

This role may be utilized in a supervisory capacity based on agency needs.

Benefits Of Employment With The State Of Indiana

The State of Indiana offers a comprehensive benefit package for full-time employees which includes:

Three (3) medical plan options (including RX coverage) as well as vision and dental plans
Wellness Rewards Program: Complete wellness activities to earn gift card rewards
Health savings account, which includes bi-weekly state contribution
Deferred compensation 457(b) account (similar to 401(k) plan) with employer match
Two (2) fully-funded pension plan options
A robust, comprehensive program of leave policies covering a variety of employee needs, including but not limited to:
150 hours of paid New Parent Leave and up to eight weeks of paid Childbirth Recovery Leave for eligible mothers
Up to 15 hours of paid community service leave

Combined 180 hours of paid vacation, personal, and sick leave time off
12 paid holidays, 14 on election years
Education Reimbursement Program
Group life insurance
Referral Bonus program
Employee assistance program that allows for covered behavioral health visits
Qualified employer for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program
Free Parking for most positions
Free LinkedIn Learning access

Equal Employment Opportunity

Reasonable accommodations may be available to enable individuals with disabilities to complete the application and interview process as well as perform the essential functions of a role. Über Uns:

Wir sind die WhereGroup - ein dynamisches, wachsendes Software-Haus für Geoinformationssysteme. Grundlage unseres Schaffens ist der Open-Source-Gedanke. Zu unseren Kunden gehören vor allem größere Behörden, Unternehmen aus verschiedenen Bereichen (Energie, Transport, Telekommunikation, Landwirtschaft, Sicherheit u. a.) und Kommunen. Von der Ist-Analyse über die Planung und Softwareentwicklung bis zum produktiven Betrieb betreuen wir alle Phasen von GIS- und Datenbank-Projekten. Unser Leistungsspektrum umfasst Geoinformationssysteme für komplexe Systemlandschaften, individuelle WebGIS-Lösungen, angepasste OpenStreetMap-Karten, mobile Anwendungen und kommunale Geoportale.

Aufgaben:

Du planst und entwickelst mit unseren Kunden Geoinformationssysteme auf Basis von QGIS.
Du arbeitest in anspruchsvollen GIS-Projekten zu spannenden Themen, wie z.B. den Ausbau Erneuerbarer Energien und dem Infrastrukturausbau.
Du unterstützt Kunden dabei, proprietäre Software durch Open-Source-Software zu ersetzen und sorgst für die Digitale Souveränität der Projekte.
Du bringst Dich in die Konzeption ein und setzt diese um.
Du unterstützt die Neu-/Weiterentwicklung, Optimierung und Pflege des Codes.
Du übernimmst Verantwortung für die Umsetzung von Modulen.
Du arbeitest in agilen Projektteams und verantwortest den Erfolg der Teams mit.
Du unterstützt die Teams in der Projektabwicklung, im Testing & in der QS.
Unser Tech-Stack im QGIS-Team besteht in erster Linie aus Python, PyQGIS, PostgreSQL, PostGIS.

Qualifikationen:

Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der praktischen Arbeit mit QGIS und der Anpassung von QGIS.
Fundierte Kenntnisse in der Softwareentwicklung mit Python und PyQGIS.
Fundierte Kenntnisse in der Konfiguration von QGIS und der Entwicklung von QGIS-Plugins.
Abgeschlossene Ausbildung oder Studium im Bereich Naturwissenschaften, Ingenieurwesen, IT oder vergleichbar.
Du zeigst Eigeninitiative.
Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse.

Wir Bieten:

Unser zehnköpfiges QGIS-Team mit einer tief verwurzelten Leidenschaft für QGIS, umfangreicher und vielseitiger Expertise sowie spannenden Projekten aus allen möglichen Themenbereichen und Branchen.

Job Description

This Opportunity

What if you could shape built and natural environments and the future of those who depend on them? At WSP, you can. WSP is currently seeking an Environmental Engineer
to join our Earth & Environment team in either Indianapolis, IN, Fort Wayne, IN, Chicago, IL, Detroit, MI, or Valparaiso, IN
. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to technically challenging site investigation and remediation projects supporting energy sector clients throughout northern Indiana.

At WSP, you'll have the opportunity to do the kind of work the world needs while collaborating with some of the brightest minds in the industry. You'll work on projects that positively impact communities and the environment while building a career as unique as you. We foster a culture that is open, curious, passionate, and adaptable, where diverse perspectives drive innovation and complex challenges inspire growth. With access to global expertise, meaningful project experiences, and opportunities for continuous development, you'll find the support and flexibility to grow your skills, expand your career, and make a lasting impact. Here, you can thrive on challenges, work alongside talented professionals, and create a future you're proud of. With us, you can

We are seeking a motivated candidate who is eager to learn and join our current multi-disciplinary team in executing technically challenging site investigation and remediation projects for our energy clients primarily in northern Indiana.

This job opening provides an opportunity to progress your career while working for an established environmental consulting firm that values employee enthusiasm, technical excellence, and professional growth. We encourage you to apply for this opportunity.

Your Impact

This position involves the implementation of project work associated with multimedia (air, water, soil, and biota) investigations and remediation. The position requires work at project sites, around construction equipment, drilling rigs, and environmental contamination. The selected candidate needs to be a self-starter, open to learning, adaptable to change, have a strong work ethic, and thrive in a dynamic environment with multiple priorities.

This position offers the opportunity to learn from and grow with an established team while addressing complex environmental challenges through the following responsibilities:

Approximately 70% field work and travel with overnight stays. Travel can include weeks at a time or a few days per week.
Perform environmental sampling (e.g., surface water, groundwater, soil, sediment, soil vapor, indoor air) and oversee subcontractors in the field (e.g., drillers).
Complete detailed field notes and other forms of documentation to accurately capture field activities and observations.
Collaborate in a team environment and communicate effectively with staff across multiple disciplines.
Communicate professionally with staff, management, clients, regulators, and on-site personnel both verbally and in writing.
Assist with project planning and coordination with laboratories, drillers, and equipment vendors.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

B.S. in Environmental Engineering or related field.
1+ years of relevant experience in environmental sampling, site investigation, or remediation.
Must be organized and detail-oriented.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Flexible to work outside normal business hours, at locations requiring overnight stays, and overtime as needed.
Ability to apply analytical and scientific thinking to define and solve problems.
Ability to work effectively in a team environment, follow detailed instructions, and learn new skills.
Ability to remain on feet for extended periods of time, either stationary or walking.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.
Must be able to pass a HAZWOPER physical and be medically able to wear a tight-fitting respirator.
Must successfully complete and pass WSP's Motor Vehicle screening.
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification required.
Experience in site investigations required.
Valid driver's license required.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience using and maintaining field equipment (e.g., groundwater pumps, field meters).
Regulatory experience in Indiana and Michigan.

WSP Benefits:

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation:

Expected Salary (all locations): $74,100 - $92,600

WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Manager
new_jobs.description:
Work for Indiana

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About The Department Of Natural Resources (DNR)

The Indiana Department of Natural Resources protects, enhances, preserves, and wisely uses natural, cultural, and recreational resources for the benefit of Indiana's citizens through professional leadership, management, and education. The Indiana Division of Historic Preservation and Archaeology promotes the conservation of Indiana's cultural resources through public education efforts, financial incentives including several grant and tax credit programs, and the administration of state and federally mandated legislation.

Role Overview

The Historic Structures Reviewer performs regulatory reviews under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, the National Environmental Policy Act, and Sections 14, 16, and 18 of IC 14-21-1. The reviewer collaborates with government officials, staff, and the public to evaluate the effects of Federal or state actions on historic properties and seek ways to avoid, minimize and mitigate impacts to cultural resources. The Historic Structures Reviewer also participates in education and outreach to educate others about historic preservation. Applicants must meet the Secretary of the Interior's Professional Qualification Standards through a combination of education and experience in the history, architecture and/or preservation field.

Role Requirements

Bachelor or Graduate degree from an accredited university or college in historic preservation, architectural history, art history, public history, preservation law, or a closely related field.
At least two (2) years of experience in research, writing, or teaching in American architectural history or restoration architecture.
Related certifications and coursework may be considered for education or experience.
Knowledge of, and ability to apply federal and state historic preservation statutes, regulations, standards, and criteria.
Knowledge of, and ability to apply the Secretary of the Interior's "Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties" (36 C.F.R. Part 68) and applicable guidelines.
Knowledge of U.S. and Indiana history and architectural history.
Ability to interpret technical drawings, construction plans, schematics, topographic maps, and floor plans.
Ability to prepare documents for administrative and regulatory action.
Excellent research and writing skills for preparing accurate, precise, clear, and thorough reports.
Ability to respond to technical inquiries from staff, project applicants, other local state and federal agencies, consultants, and the general public
Ability to use SHAARD database of information on historical, architectural, and archaeological resources in Indiana and familiarity using GIS systems
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Be willing to travel with reasonable accommodation.

Salary

The salary for this position traditionally starts at $53,222.00 but may be commensurate with education and work experience. Use our Compensation Calculator
to view the total compensation package.

A Day In The Life

The essential functions of this role are as follows:

Serves as an environmental expert and provides guidance to regulated communities, government officials, attorneys and staff responsible for a variety of programs and program elements.
Project Management: Performs project management duties to ensure effective and timely management of program area needs, attends meetings, and responds to telephone calls, e-mails, etc., as required. Acts as a technical point-of-contact for assigned programs administering environmental programs which may include, but not limited to, environmental media sampling, data analysis, technical writing, work plan and report preparation, technical reviews, etc.
Permits: Researches state and federal guidance, laws, and regulations related to permits. Contacts applicants to request additional information to process applications, when necessary. Responds to comments from applicants, defends permit terms and conditions, and interacts with permittees to resolve permitting issues. Attends and participates in public meetings and hearings regarding permit actions throughout Indiana and/or appears in legal appeals of permit actions.
Inspection: Conducts surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, reads plans, interprets findings, and cites appropriate violations of state and federal regulations. Provides technical and regulatory guidance to the regulated community in their assigned geographic area.
Enforcement & Compliance: Uses all compliance, enforcement tools, and resources available to ensure that regulated sources return to compliance with state and federal laws, regulations, and standards in a timely manner.
Support Services: Works to support the various programs in assigned agency in multiple capacities.
Sampling: Assists with the preparation of sampling and analysis work plans. Conducts field work as necessary following agency/section Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for assigned sites.
Technical Analysis & Testing: Conducts technical analysis and/or provides technical insights to assess environmental impacts with goals to meet state and national regulations.
Outreach Coordination: Communicates effectively with responsible parties, consultants, and/or their representatives, affected stakeholders, and interested parties such as citizens, public officials, and interest groups in a courteous and professional manner regarding permits, laws, questions, and program-related inquiries.
Essential functions of this position require travel on most workdays to inspect, audit, examine, survey, or investigate clients, customers, or other regulated entities and write reports at various sites depending on business needs. Employee reports to the agency’s office for occasional meetings or events. Number and timing of work hours may vary daily or weekly to accommodate operational needs and staffing concerns at the client’s or customer’s worksite, minimize expenditures for repeated visits to complete the work, and allocate resources to complete assigned work effectively.

The job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

This position is exempt from overtime compensation for additional work hours which may be required to complete essential functions or other assigned work. Exempt employees may work more than 75 hours in a pay period without additional compensation and must report a minimum of 75 hours per pay period of work hours and/or paid leave taken to receive their base biweekly salary.

What You'll Need For Success

Individuals in this role should minimally be able to articulate or demonstrate the following:

Broad knowledge of theories, environmental protection principles and practices, specialty area, and program area.
Thorough knowledge of chemistry, biology, hydrology, mathematics, engineering, and other environmental sciences as they relate to program area.
Thorough knowledge of soil, water, air sampling, laboratory analysis and interpretation as it relates to program area.
Ability to conduct surveys, inspections and investigations of facilities and sites, review projects/situations, read plans, interpret findings, and make recommendations.
Ability to prepare documents for administrative and regulatory action.
Excellent research and writing skills for preparing accurate, precise, clear, and thorough reports.
Ability to effectively interact and orally communicate with parties with diverse levels of environmental expertise particularly for purposes of meetings, hearings, and negotiating critically sensitive issues.
Ability to interpret and apply legal terminology and practices, and the ability to apply these in a variety of conditions and situations.

A degree is not required. However, at least five (5) years of environmental or environmental public health experience applying the outlined knowledge, skills, and abilities in a similar role may be considered.

Individuals should have the ability to perform essential functions with or without reasonable accommodation.

Supervisory Responsibilities/Direct Reports

This role may be utilized in a supervisory capacity based on agency needs.

Benefits Of Employment With The State Of Indiana

The State of Indiana offers a comprehensive benefit package for full-time employees which includes:

Three (3) medical plan options (including RX coverage) as well as vision and dental plans
Wellness Rewards Program: Complete wellness activities to earn gift card rewards
Health savings account, which includes bi-weekly state contribution
Deferred compensation 457(b) account (similar to 401(k) plan) with employer match
Two (2) fully-funded pension plan options

12 paid holidays, 14 on election years

Qualified employer for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program

Job Summary

To conduct engineering reviews of Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) plans that accompany all new or renewed Individual National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) program permits for Stormwater discharges associated with construction activities for the regulated community as well as under agreements with Municipalities or other governmental agencies in accordance with the applicable laws, rules and regulations, policies, and procedures.

Essential Job Functions

Provides education and outreach service on the PCSM and NPDES Programs.
Maintains a system for receipt, assessment, and resolution of PCSM complaints associated with active NPDES permitted sites prior to the submittal and acknowledgement of the Notice of Termination (NOT).
Receive, process, and conduct engineering reviews, as a Registered Pennsylvania Professional Engineer (PE), of PCSM plans that accompany all new or renewed Individual Permits for Stormwater Discharges Associated with Construction Activities that have been designed in accordance with the PA Stormwater Best Management Practice (BMP) Manual or that have been developed using standards and design criteria other than those in the PA Stormwater BMP Manual.
Provide PCSM plan reviews under agreements with municipalities or other governmental agencies in accordance with the applicable laws, rules and regulations, policies and procedures.
Conducts inspections of PCSM BMPs and make notes in the standard inspection report forms when on site performing E&S Program duties during the construction phase of the project and conduct a final inspection in conjunction with a Notice of Termination.
Conducts and forwards all complaints related to PCSM BMPs to the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Regional Office Service Representative when construction is complete and a Notice of Termination has been acknowledged.
Coordinate with Ag/PCSM Engineer on review findings after review of PCSM plans.
Provides technical assistance to contractors, technicians, etc.
Performs other job-related duties as required.

Bachelor’s degree in engineering required. PE exam completion and PE license required. Must maintain current registration as a Professional Engineer in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP USA is Seeking a Senior Technical Environmental Compliance Specialist
for our Atlanta, GA location
.

Protects the Department of Aviation by ensuring compliance with applicable federal, state, regional, and local environmental laws, regulations, permits, and regulatory requirements. Serves as the Department's senior technical authority for environmental compliance and leads the execution of regulatory compliance programs supporting airport operations and capital improvement projects. Primary responsibilities include stormwater, wastewater, surface water quality, industrial discharges, deicing-related discharges, spill prevention and response, environmental monitoring, inspections, reporting, regulatory coordination, and construction-related environmental compliance.

Your Impact

Manages environmental compliance activities associated with stormwater, wastewater, surface water quality, industrial discharges, deicing operations, construction stormwater, spill prevention, spill response, and related regulatory requirements.
Provides technical leadership for permit compliance, inspections, environmental monitoring, reporting, corrective actions, regulatory notifications, and compliance documentation.
Reviews permits, regulations, agency guidance, technical data, engineering documents, construction plans, and operational changes to identify compliance risks.
Coordinates with regulatory agencies, airport departments, consultants, contractors, tenants, and airlines to ensure compliance obligations are implemented.
Directs field investigations, inspections, and corrective actions.
Supports capital improvement projects through environmental reviews, SWPPP implementation, erosion and sediment control oversight, construction inspections, and contractor environmental compliance.
Independently interprets environmental regulations, permit requirements, technical standards, and agency guidance to develop compliance strategies, evaluate environmental risks, recommend corrective actions, prioritize field activities, and support Department decision-making.
Provides senior technical direction to consultants, contractors, inspectors, airport staff, and multidisciplinary project teams.
Directs technical work, coordinates compliance activities, and monitors performance against regulatory requirements, permit conditions, schedules, and Department priorities.
This position does not include formal personnel-management responsibilities.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, Biology, Chemistry, Natural Resources, or a related field.
7 to 10 years of progressively responsible experience in environmental compliance, environmental permitting, stormwater management, wastewater compliance, water quality monitoring, environmental engineering, regulatory compliance, or a closely related field.
Experience must include leading complex technical assignments, managing regulatory compliance activities, and directing or coordinating the work of consultants, contractors, inspectors, or multidisciplinary project teams.
Comprehensive knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations; Clean Water Act; NPDES permitting; industrial stormwater; wastewater pretreatment; Georgia construction stormwater requirements; erosion and sediment control; environmental monitoring; environmental auditing; regulatory reporting; and construction compliance.
Strong analytical, communication, organizational, problem-solving, and technical leadership skills.
Valid Georgia driver's license required.

Experience supporting airport, transportation, municipal, industrial, utility, or other large public infrastructure environmental compliance programs.
Experience with FAA-funded capital projects, NPDES permitting, MS4 programs, Georgia EPD regulations, environmental auditing, and consultant management is preferred.
